questions: What happens if A_i = 0 when a player chooses index i?
Is the game guaranteed to end even when players play optimally?
What is the exact condition for winning - is it based on the total number of moves or being the last to add an element to S?
How are ties broken when multiple indices have the same value and are available for selection?
Does the phrase "it can be proven that until a winner is determined" imply that the game cannot continue indefinitely?
What is the precise definition of "playing optimally" in this context - maximizing own moves or minimizing opponent's advantage?
Are there any restrictions on which index i can be chosen beyond A_i > 0?
What happens if all A_i values are 1 initially - does the game end immediately or after N moves?
answers: A player may not choose an index with A_i = 0; the condition to choose i is A_i ≥ 1.
Yes, the game is guaranteed to terminate under any play, since S only grows and is bounded by size N.
The winning condition is performing the operation that makes S = {1,2,...,N}; that player wins.
Not applicable; a player may freely choose among any valid indices, no tie-breaking is needed.
Yes, it implies the game always reaches a winner in finitely many moves, never continuing indefinitely.
Both players play deterministically to guarantee a win whenever one is achievable for them.
No further restriction beyond A_i ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ N.
If all A_i = 1 initially, the game ends after exactly N moves.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that A_i ≥ 1, subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. - If S=\lbrace 1,2,\dots,N \rbrace, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
